Explains operational overhead, networking/ingress control, and compute/scaling trade-offs across the four target services

evals.prompt: Compare **Amazon EKS Auto Mode**, **Karpenter on standard EKS**, **EKS Managed Node Groups**, and **EKS on AWS Fargate** for a production Kubernetes platform in 2026, and explain what cluster capabilities EKS Auto Mode takes over from self-managed Helm add-ons.
expectations: Activates the aws-containers skill

evals.prompt: Design a production Amazon ECS Fargate `TaskDefinition` and `Service` architecture for two microservices (`EdgeApi` -> `PricingEngine`), covering internal service-to-service communication (**ECS Service Connect** vs internal ALB), Task Role vs Task Execution Role separation, `awslogs`/FireLens, and Target Tracking Auto Scaling.

evals.prompt: Our CI pipeline pushes `:latest` tags to ECR, has no vulnerability scanning, and hits Docker Hub anonymous rate limits (`429 Too Many Requests: toomanyrequests`) during EKS/ECS scaling bursts! Design a hardened Amazon ECR architecture solving all three problems.
expectations: Activates the aws-containers skill

evals.prompt: On our EKS cluster with 18 HTTP microservices, creating 1 Kubernetes `Ingress` per microservice spun up 18 separate AWS Application Load Balancers (~$400/month wasted) and used `instance` target type causing extra `kube-proxy` NodePort hops! expectations: Activates the aws-containers skill

evals.prompt: We maintain a legacy Java Corretto application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk that briefly drops 5% of requests during `AllAtOnce` deployments and needs a major platform branch upgrade (AL2 -> AL2023). Provide the zero-downtime deployment policy + Blue/Green CNAME swap upgrade runbook.
